points.text: Broader impact of Pass@k inference unclear; should discuss application in LLM inference/generation.
Experiments do not show BoM benefiting from scaling monotonicity; accuracy drops or stays flat with N.
Technical terms (coverage constant, Assumptions 3.1/3.2) need more intuitive explanation.
Choice of alpha values in experiments, differing by N, is not explained.
No analysis of how accuracy varies with alpha.
Missing precise comparison with Aminian et al. BoN regret upper bound.
No empirical or conceptual comparison to InfAlign.
No theoretical or empirical comparison to Soft-BoN.
Theorem 4.2 regret tends to N-independent constant; mechanism and implications need elaboration.
Unclear whether reward function is calibrated in theory or experiments.
Criterion for 'mathematical equivalence' of answers is undefined.
Negative results for BoN/majority vote are worst-case pathological; instance-dependent bounds would be stronger.
BoM requires alpha tied to unknown pi_ref(y*|x) and per-prompt N threshold; no practical way to set them.
No discussion of how alpha used in experiments was chosen.
No ablation of alpha values on performance.
Dependence on N missing in Theorems 5.1 and 6.1, unlike Huang et al.
BoM upper bound and minimax lower bound do not depend on N, missing compute-regret trade-off.
Theorem 5.1 does not cover regime k <~ N <~ C*.
Unclear how performance scales with response alphabet size.
Algorithm requires knowledge of C*(x) to ensure N is large enough.
Algorithm requires knowledge of lower bound on reward-model error, which is cumbersome.
Unique-optimum assumption restrictive; many tasks have multiple correct answers or near-ties.
BoM threshold depends on unknown C*; no estimator or misspecification analysis.
Empirical scope narrow: only math/verifier-style datasets.
Novelty claim overstated; BoN non-monotonicity already shown by Huang et al.; Stroebl et al. close.
Minimax lower bounds use graded-reward hard instances, not the binary Pass@k setting.
Brown et al. (2024) characterization appears inaccurate.
Pass@k metric origin should cite the Codex paper, not AlphaCode.
Assumption 3.1 not mapped to experimental group-mean reward; no empirical reward error estimate.
Unknown C* and per-prompt thresholds vs single global alpha; adaptive rule needed.
Sensitivity of accuracy to alpha not reported.
Implicit unique-correct-answer assumption fails for proofs and code.
Stationary reward-error assumption unrealistic; RMs err on rare fluent-but-wrong answers.
Prompt-by-prompt analysis ignores heterogeneity of C*(x) for average accuracy.
No experiment on task with multiple correct answers such as code.
Reward-model cost accounting unclear; no accuracy vs total compute curves.
Ignores ready tools like top-k identification, confidence-bound ranking, conformal selection.
Setting presentation confusing: contradictory sentence, implicit notation identifications.
Abstract claim that BoN lacks k-scaling contradicts Table 1 'Unknown'.
Non-degradation with N shown only above threshold and in one figure.
No variance or intervals; small AIME24 differences uninterpretable.
Appendix C referenced for additional models is empty.
Alpha used in experiments should be stated.
No limitations or future-work discussion.
Typos and grammar errors (GSK8K, Section 3).
Optimality requires alpha from unknown C*; guarantee is oracle-parameterized.
Experiments use global alpha with no stated selection protocol or validation split.
Abstract claim about BoN k-scaling contradicted by Table 1, Section 4.2, Remark 4.3.
Hard instances use graded rewards while motivating Pass@k case is binary.
Experiments cannot verify worst-case monotonicity claims; single instance, saturating explanation.
Missing reward-weighted voting and min-support BoN baselines to isolate frequency threshold.
Scaling monotonicity misinterpreted as non-degradation; Theorem 5.1 vacuous below N threshold.
Claim BoM queries filtered subset conflicts with Algorithm 3 querying all N.
Chernoff constants in Appendix B.2/B.3 do not follow.
Theorem 6.1 statement misses condition ensuring delta <= 1.
Referenced additional-model results in Appendix C are empty.
Theorem 4.1 condition excludes hard-threshold weighted voting.
Guarantee needs unknown per-prompt C*; one global alpha cannot match it.
Alpha selection protocol unstated; no validation split; values missing for k-sweeps.
No alpha sensitivity sweep across datasets.
Experiments cannot verify scaling-monotonic claims; Figure 3 one small dataset, few N.
No seeds, variance or confidence intervals.
Theoretical sqrt(1/k) rate never fit or plotted.
Missing weighted majority voting and regularized/pessimistic BoN baselines.
Experimental BoN ranks answer groups by mean reward, differing from Algorithm 2.
Theory regime C* >= 2k mismatches experiments where most prompts are easy.
Appendix B.2/B.3 constants contain slips.
Efficiency claim contradicts Algorithm 3 querying all responses.
Condition for second regret term dominating stated incorrectly.
Typos and notation issues (GSK8K, undefined A(x), k vs N, Section 3 sentence).

P.summary: Broader practical impact of Pass@k inference unclear.
Experiments do not show BoM improving or monotone with N.
Choice of alpha in experiments unexplained.
No ablation/sensitivity of accuracy to alpha.
Missing comparison with Aminian et al. BoN regret bounds.
Theorem 4.2 asymptotic constant regret needs explanation.
Lower bounds are worst-case pathological, not instance-dependent.
BoM hyperparameters depend on unknown C* and reward error; no practical estimation.
Bounds lack dependence on N, missing compute-regret trade-off.
Theorem 5.1 does not cover k <~ N <~ C* regime.
Scaling with response alphabet size unclear.
Empirical scope limited to math datasets.

Q.summary: Novelty overstated relative to Huang et al. and Stroebl et al.
Lower bounds rely on graded rewards, not binary Pass@k.
Reward assumption not grounded in experimental reward model.
Guarantee needs unknown per-prompt C*; global alpha; no adaptive rule.
Alpha selection protocol in experiments unstated.
No experiment on multi-answer tasks like code.
Related tools from other fields not considered.
Non-degradation with N overstated; theorem vacuous below threshold.
Experiments cannot verify worst-case monotonicity claims.
Missing weighted voting and regularized/min-support BoN baselines.
Incorrect condition for regret term dominance.
